screening_decisions.reason: Clomipramine is a tricyclic, but the route is intravenous, not oral as required by the criteria.
Fluoxetine is a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI), not a tricyclic drug.
Nortriptyline is a tricyclic; the study is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in depressed adolescents (12\\u201317 years) using oral dosing.
This is a qualitative review article, not a randomized controlled trial.

Imipramine is a tricyclic; this is described as a double-blind pilot study with a placebo group in depressed children. Although randomization is not explicitly stated, the double-blind controlled design in children with depression makes it highly likely to be a small RCT. Included conservatively.
Amitriptyline is a tricyclic; this is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial in children aged 9\\u201312 years with major depressive disorder, using oral dosing.
This is a Cochrane review, not a single randomized controlled trial.

Imipramine is a tricyclic; this is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in adolescents with comorbid major depressive disorder and anxiety. Both arms received CBT, so the comparison remains imipramine versus placebo. Population meets the \'depressed people\' criterion.

Imipramine is a tricyclic; a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial explicitly described with random assignment. Population is prepubertal children with major depressive disorder (oral dosing).
This three-arm RCT includes an imipramine (tricyclic) arm together with a placebo arm, allowing a direct TCA-versus-placebo comparison in depressed adolescents. Oral route is used.
Review/discussion article on mechanisms of action; not a randomized controlled trial.
This is a safety review of SSRI overdoses; not an RCT, and irrelevant to TCA vs placebo in depression.
Methodological paper about heterogeneity in meta-analyses; not an RCT.
Observational case series of accidental amitriptyline poisoning; not an RCT.
This is a secondary analysis of pooled data from earlier trials. It is not a standalone randomized controlled trial.
Desipramine is a tricyclic; this is a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in adolescents (13\\u201318) with major depressive disorder, using oral desipramine.
Review/discussion paper; not an RCT.

The described double-blind study uses imipramine but the population is school-refusing children with anxiety/depression symptoms; it is not explicitly stated that all participants were clinically depressed (i.e., had major depressive disorder). Therefore the \'depressed people\' criterion is not clearly met.
Retrospective study of accidental tricyclic ingestions; not an RCT.
Amitriptyline is a tricyclic; this is an RCT comparing oral amitriptyline with placebo in depressed adolescents (12\\u201317 years).
Although clomipramine is a tricyclic and the study is a double-blind trial, the population is children with school phobia/neurotic disorder, not specifically depression.
This is a meta-analysis of adult studies (age 18\\u201365); not an RCT in the 6\\u201318 age range, and not a primary trial.
This is a non-randomized, open-label study of imipramine plasma levels and clinical response; not a randomized placebo-controlled trial.
Amitriptyline is a tricyclic; this is an RCT comparing oral amitriptyline with placebo in adolescents with treatment-resistant major depressive disorder.
This is a secondary analysis of compliance and side-effect data from the trial reported in study 8. It does not present primary efficacy outcomes and is not an independent RCT.
